title: Colder. Less growth?
factual_caveat: The 2015 trial studied repeated approximately 10°C cold-water immersion for 10 minutes immediately after twice-weekly lower-body resistance sessions over 12 weeks. Twenty-four young trained men enrolled and 21 were analyzed. It does not establish effects of ordinary cold showers, every use of cold, or an exact safe timing threshold. The 2024 eight-study synthesis suggests attenuated hypertrophy but study quality limits confidence. The frozen-lake stock clip is illustrative and does not reproduce the trial setting or water temperature.

sources.title: Post-exercise cold water immersion attenuates acute anabolic signalling and long-term adaptations in muscle to strength training
sources.design: Randomized trial; chronic-training component: 24 enrolled, 21 analyzed; physically active young men with at least 12 months of strength-training experience; 12 weeks; twice-weekly lower-body training; 10 minutes of approximately 10°C immersion or low-intensity cycling after sessions.
sources.claim_scope: The active-recovery group showed greater gains in measured muscle mass and strength. These findings concern this repeated post-training protocol, not all forms of cold exposure.

sources.title: Throwing cold water on muscle growth: A systematic review with meta-analysis of the effects of postexercise cold water immersion on resistance training-induced hypertrophy
sources.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis; eight studies.
sources.claim_scope: Immediate post-training immersion may attenuate muscle hypertrophy. Relatively fair-to-poor study quality limits certainty.

human_recording_script: Your recovery routine and your muscle-building goal can pull in different directions. In a twelve-week trial, twenty-one trained men finished lifting with either ten minutes of cold-water immersion or easy cycling. The cycling group gained more muscle and strength. A later review also found that cold immersion soon after lifting may reduce muscle growth, though the studies had limitations. This is about repeated cold immersion straight after training. It does not prove that an occasional cold shower ruins your progress.
human_delivery_direction: A calm, curious training partner. Open with mild surprise, explain the protocol plainly, and slow down for the limit. Do not perform an ice-bath challenge or imitate a named person. This script is a future recording brief; it is not present in the voice-free preview audio.
